note.en: No new standalone Neural Media book or essay from K has appeared in 2026 so far. This year's activity is posts, interviews, talks, an exhibition, a book release and papers by other writers that cite K's neural media essays. Items tagged “Wider context” are either K's recent activity that isn't about neural media itself, or related work by others that doesn't directly engage K's framework. Dates are shown in China time (UTC+8), so US-dated posts can appear one day later.
note.zh: 截至目前，K 在 2026 年尚未发表新的「神经媒体」专著或独立文章。今年的动态主要是社交媒体帖子、访谈、演讲、展览、一本新书的发行，以及其他作者引用 K 神经媒体文章的论文。标为「相关背景」的条目，或是并非专门讨论神经媒体的 K 的近期动态，或是未直接讨论 K 理论框架的其他人的相关工作。所有日期均按北京时间（UTC+8）显示，因此美国时间发布的帖子可能会显示为晚一天。

title.en: Neural Media
title.zh: 神经媒体

intro.en: Everything we can find on K Allado-McDowell's concept of Neural Media: AI-era media that sense us, model us and generate content back at us. Videos, posts, essays, interviews, podcasts, talks, exhibitions and books in one timeline, newest first.
intro.zh: 这里汇集了关于 K Allado-McDowell「神经媒体」（Neural Media）概念的全部资料。神经媒体指 AI 时代那些感知我们、为我们建模，并反过来向我们生成内容的媒介。视频、帖子、文章、访谈、播客、演讲、展览和图书都收在同一条时间线上，最新的排在最前。

lead.en: K splits media into four types. Each takes about 30 years to go from birth to maturity, when it becomes the dominant form, and each is defined by a kind of space, a kind of content and a kind of identity.
lead.zh: K 把媒介分为四种类型。每种类型从诞生到成熟、成为主导媒介大约需要 30 年，并各自对应一种空间、一种内容和一种身份。

identity.zh: 把人归入不同的人口统计群体。

identity.en: Lets people build their own identity.
Treats us as “embeddings”: points in an AI system's statistical map that sense us, model us and generate content back at us.
identity.zh: 把我们当作「嵌入」（embedding），也就是 AI 系统统计图谱中的一个个点。这些系统感知我们、为我们建模，并反过来向我们生成内容。

notes.en: The neural phase also covers brain-computer interfaces and biological computing.
notes.zh: 神经媒体阶段还涵盖脑机接口与生物计算。

notes.en: By K's timeline it is only half-formed, so it can still be shaped.
notes.zh: 按照 K 的时间线，这一阶段才走到一半，因此仍有被塑造的空间。

notes.en: K's hope: point it at ecology and nonhuman intelligence, not just at modelling people.
notes.zh: K 希望让它面向生态与非人类智能，而不只是用来为人建模。

title.en: On Neural Media: K Allado-McDowell at Long Now
title.zh: 《论神经媒体》：K Allado-McDowell 在 Long Now 的演讲

meta.en: Recorded 25 Feb 2025 at the Cowell Theatre, San Francisco · 54:25 · the fullest version of the framework
meta.zh: 2025 年 2 月 25 日录制于旧金山 Cowell 剧场 · 54 分 25 秒 · 该框架最完整的阐述

takeaways.en: K coined the term while making a neuro-opera in which brain waves controlled AI-generated visuals.
takeaways.zh: K 是在创作一部「神经歌剧」时提出这个术语的。在那部作品中，脑电波实时控制着 AI 生成的影像。

takeaways.en: K reads low-quality AI “slop” as the statistical average of style and ideology.
takeaways.zh: K 把低质量的 AI「垃圾内容」（slop）解读为风格与意识形态的统计平均值。

takeaways.en: Systems for credit, insurance and dating increasingly treat us as embeddings.
takeaways.zh: 信用、保险和约会等系统越来越多地把我们当作「嵌入」来对待。

takeaways.en: K's hopeful path runs through projects like Project CETI's whale research and SPUN's maps of fungal networks.
takeaways.zh: K 看到的希望，体现在 Project CETI 的鲸类研究和 SPUN 绘制的真菌网络地图等项目中。

title.en: CHANEL Center for Artists and Technology (CCAT) Speaker Series: Barry Threw & K Allado-McDowell, CalArts
title.zh: 加州艺术学院 CHANEL 艺术与技术中心（CCAT）演讲系列：Barry Threw 与 K Allado-McDowell

summary.en: K joins curator and Gray Area director Barry Threw at CalArts’ Bijou Theater (4:30–6 PM) for a CCAT Speaker Series conversation on how emerging technology enables creativity and the institutional infrastructures that support artistic experimentation, followed by a Q&A moderated by Robin Xie (MFA Film Directing). Wider context: this is K’s recent activity, not specifically about neural media.
summary.zh: K 与策展人、旧金山 Gray Area 艺术总监 Barry Threw 一同出席加州艺术学院 Bijou 剧场的 CCAT 演讲系列（下午 4:30–6:00），对谈新兴技术如何赋能创作，以及支撑艺术实验的制度基础；随后由电影导演 MFA 学生 Robin Xie 主持问答。（相关背景：这是 K 的近期动态，并非专门讨论神经媒体。）

title.en: K on X: explorations of neuralese approach neural media “on their own terms”
title.zh: K 在 X 上发帖：探索 neuralese，就是「按神经媒体自身的方式」去理解它们

summary.en: K describes explorations of neuralese as approaching neural media “as a high dimensional outside beyond human language, as maps of the virtual translated for us, not (yet) directly perceptible.”
summary.zh: K 写道，对 neuralese 的探索是把神经媒体当作「人类语言之外的高维外部，当作为我们翻译过来的虚拟地图，（尚）不能被直接感知」来理解。

title.en: K on X: neural media are made of network media
title.zh: K 在 X 上发帖：神经媒体由网络媒体构成

summary.en: “The language of the embedded subject is made of memetic pointers because neural media are made of network media (like tv was once made of theater).”
summary.zh: 「嵌入式主体的语言由模因指针构成，因为神经媒体由网络媒体构成（就像电视曾经由戏剧构成）。」

title.en: K on X: “BCI x AI = neural media”
title.zh: K 在 X 上发帖：「脑机接口 × AI = 神经媒体」

summary.en: Quoting a thread on neuroAI (AI scaling laws applied to brain-computer interfaces), K restates that BCIs combined with AI fall under neural media.
summary.zh: K 转引了一条关于 neuroAI（把 AI 的规模定律应用于脑机接口）的帖子，并重申：脑机接口与 AI 的结合属于神经媒体。

title.en: K on X: “Neuralese: what neural media speak”
title.zh: K 在 X 上发帖：「Neuralese：神经媒体所说的语言」

summary.en: K frames “neuralese”, the internal language of AI agents, as the language of neural media. This opens the run of neuralese posts.
summary.zh: K 把「neuralese」（神经语，即 AI 智能体的内部语言）定义为神经媒体的语言，由此开启了一系列关于 neuralese 的帖子。

title.en: Saturnin Pugnet, “Phase Lock”: a manifesto on brain-computer interfaces and human agency in the age of AI
title.zh: Saturnin Pugnet《Phase Lock》：关于脑机接口与 AI 时代人类能动性的宣言

summary.en: A long-form manifesto arguing that AI is outpacing humans' ability to steer it through keyboards and screens, and that brain-computer interfaces offer “alignment-by-integration”: BCI as a training signal for AI, a new interface, and a way to widen mind–machine bandwidth. It bets that AI-style scaling (hardware, data, models) applies to brain decoding, led by consumer non-invasive devices. First published 2 Oct 2026; v1.2 on 16 Oct. Wider context: it does not mention K or the term neural media, but it covers the BCI × AI convergence that K counts as part of neural media (see K's 7 Oct post “BCI x AI = neural media”).
summary.zh: 这是一篇长篇宣言，认为 AI 的发展已经超出人类用键盘和屏幕去引导它的能力，主张通过脑机接口实现“融合式对齐”：用脑机接口为 AI 提供训练信号、作为新的交互界面，并扩大大脑与机器之间的带宽。作者认为 AI 那套“更好硬件、更多数据、更大模型”的扩展规律同样适用于大脑解码，而消费级非侵入式设备会是最快的路线。2026 年 10 月 2 日首发，10 月 16 日更新至 v1.2。（相关背景：文中没有提到 K 或“神经媒体”一词，但讨论的正是 K 归入神经媒体的“脑机接口 × AI”融合，参见 K 10 月 7 日的推文“BCI x AI = neural media”。）

LAS and DISTANZ first launched it in April 2024. Wider context: this is K's recent activity, not specifically about neural media.

summary.en: “‘Slop’ aka the low-effort, high-volume AI-generated content, asks an urgent question: what happens when human expression can be reproduced at scale?” Long Now posted this on X and LinkedIn, pointing to K's essay.
summary.zh: 「所谓 slop，就是低投入、大批量的 AI 生成内容，它提出了一个紧迫的问题：当人类的表达可以被大规模复制时，会发生什么？」Long Now 在 X 和 LinkedIn 上发布了这段话，并附上 K 的文章链接。

title.en: K on X: why “neural media” needs its own name
title.zh: K 在 X 上回应：为什么「神经媒体」需要一个独立的名称

summary.en: Replying to a reader who questioned the term under Long Now's slop post, K wrote that “neural media's accelerated feedback loops affect our psyches much more powerfully than previous forms, which is why the distinction matters”. In a follow-up the next day K added that these differences “warrant a new framing”.
summary.zh: 有读者在 Long Now 关于 AI 垃圾内容的帖子下质疑这个术语。K 回复说，神经媒体加速的反馈回路对我们心理的影响远比以往的媒介形式强烈，所以这个区分很重要。次日 K 又补充说，这些差异值得用一个新的框架来理解。

title.en: Caroline Busta & Lil Internet, “On Neural Media and the Re-Organisation of Culture”, Vienna Digital Cultures
title.zh: Caroline Busta 与 Lil Internet：《论神经媒体与文化的重组》，维也纳数字文化节

summary.en: The New Models co-founders spoke at Kunsthalle Wien Karlsplatz during Vienna Digital Cultures 2025 (5–18 May, theme “model collapse”). Busta asked how media organised by neural rather than linear or network patterns reshapes what it means to be human, using TikTok, Balenciaga and Shein as examples, then discussed with Lil Internet how algorithmic media flows create new forms of subjectivity.
summary.zh: 两位 New Models 联合创始人在 2025 年维也纳数字文化节（5 月 5 日至 18 日，主题为「模型崩溃」）期间于维也纳美术馆卡尔广场馆演讲。Busta 探讨当媒介不再按线性或网络模式、而是按神经模式组织时，人的概念会如何改变，并以 TikTok、Balenciaga 和 Shein 为例；随后与 Lil Internet 讨论算法驱动的媒介流如何催生新的主体形式和文化结构。

source.zh: museumsfernsehen / 维也纳数字文化节

summary.en: Caroline Busta and Lil Internet consider frameworks for the present and future of media, “from ‘psyop realism’ to ‘post-discursivity’ to ‘neural media’”, arguing that vibes are measurable to the machine learning that now dominates media.
summary.zh: Caroline Busta 与 Lil Internet 探讨理解当下与未来媒介的几种框架，「从“心理战现实主义”到“后话语性”，再到“神经媒体”」，并指出「氛围」对如今主导媒介的机器学习而言是可测量、可读取的。

summary.en: An interactive show with Vytas Jankauskas, Jan Zuiderveld and Joseph Wilk about living as “embedded nodes” inside intelligent systems that project versions of ourselves back to us. In the interview the curator names K Allado-McDowell’s concept of designing neural media, together with N. Katherine Hayles, as a major inspiration.
summary.zh: 这是一个互动展览，参展艺术家为 Vytas Jankauskas、Jan Zuiderveld 和 Joseph Wilk，探讨我们作为「嵌入式节点」生活在智能系统中，系统又通过预测、标注和优化把各种版本的我们投射回来。策展人在访谈中表示，K Allado-McDowell 的「设计神经媒体」概念与 N. Katherine Hayles 的理论是她的主要灵感来源。

summary.en: The Oslo design studio has a Grafill research grant to build “a theoretical framework for neural media: a cognitive, generative medium”, explicitly building on K’s ideas. Its talks include “Neural Media Starter Pack” at Klingenberg Cinema (21 May 2026) and “Storytelling in Neural Media” for Norway’s National Museum and Snøhetta (25 May 2024).
summary.zh: 这家奥斯陆设计工作室获得 Grafill 研究资助，正在建立「神经媒体（一种具有认知能力的生成式媒介）的理论框架」，明确以 K 的思想为基础。其讲座包括在 Klingenberg 影院举办的《神经媒体入门包》（2026 年 5 月 21 日），以及应挪威国家艺术、建筑与设计博物馆和 Snøhetta 之邀所做的《神经媒体中的叙事》（2024 年 5 月 25 日）。

Students make work with generative AI image, video, sound and gameplay while examining automation, labour, authorship and bias. title.en: Suk Kyoung Choi & Steve DiPaola (Simon Fraser University): an independent coinage of “neural media”
title.zh: Suk Kyoung Choi 与 Steve DiPaola（西蒙菲莎大学）：独立提出的「神经媒体」概念

summary.en: In “Artistic Style Meets Artificial Intelligence” (Journal of Perceptual Imaging, 2021, with Hannu Töyrylä) they propose a post-phenomenology of “neural media”, meaning artistic practice with deep neural networks that unsettles intention and authorship. They continued the idea in 2023 papers on generative AI as an “other” and on journeys through latent space. Wider context: a separate, earlier use of the term about artists’ process, not K’s media-eras framework.
summary.zh: 他们在《Artistic Style Meets Artificial Intelligence》（《Journal of Perceptual Imaging》，2021 年，与 Hannu Töyrylä 合著）中提出「神经媒体」的后现象学：指借助深度神经网络进行的艺术实践，这种实践会动摇创作意图与作者身份。2023 年他们又发表论文，延续讨论把生成式 AI 视为「他者」以及在潜在空间中的创作旅程。（相关背景：这是更早、独立的术语用法，关注艺术家的创作过程，而非 K 的媒介时代框架。）

title.en: Most Dismal Swamp in “The World Is Sleepwalking”, Rijeka, and at Goldsmiths

summary.en: Dane Sutherland’s project describes itself as “Multi-User Shared Hallucinations dredged from the slumgullion swamp of adversarial digital, platform, and neural media”; its work The Bastard Fields “dredges our emerging neural mediascapes”. It was shown in Daniela Cotimbo’s exhibition (Re:humanism, Mine, Yours, Ours festival, 23 Apr – 14 May 2026), and Sutherland gave a Goldsmiths Visual Cultures lecture on 16 Oct 2025. Wider context: it uses the term but does not cite K.
summary.zh: Dane Sutherland 的这个艺术项目自称是从「对抗性的数字媒体、平台媒体与神经媒体的泥沼中打捞出的多用户共享幻觉」，作品《The Bastard Fields》则「打捞我们正在形成的神经媒介景观」。作品入选 Daniela Cotimbo 策划的展览（Re:humanism，Mine, Yours, Ours 艺术节，2026 年 4 月 23 日至 5 月 14 日）；Sutherland 还于 2025 年 10 月 16 日在金史密斯学院视觉文化系演讲。（相关背景：使用了这一术语，但并未引用 K。）

title.en: Who else works on neural media
title.zh: 其他研究者与机构

lead.en: No one besides K has published a full theory of neural media. The term is now used by critics, curators, designers and schools, mostly building on K's framework; one research group coined it separately in 2021, and several scholars work on the same questions under other names. Labels show whether each source explicitly uses the term “neural media”, cites K, or is adjacent work.
lead.zh: 除 K 之外，目前还没有人发表过完整的神经媒体理论。如今这个词已被评论家、策展人、设计师和院校使用，大多以 K 的框架为基础；有一个研究团队在 2021 年独立提出了这个词，另有几位学者用其他名称研究相同的问题。标签说明每条来源是明确使用「神经媒体」一词、引用 K，还是属于相关领域的研究。
